summary: Vunisea Airport serves the southern Fijian island of Kadavu, providing the primary air link for travelers heading to this remote and largely undeveloped region. The small airport connects Kadavu to Fiji's main island Viti Levu via short domestic flights. It is the gateway to some of Fiji's most pristine diving sites, including the famous Great Astrolabe Reef.
faqs:
Q: What airlines serve Vunisea Airport?
A: Vunisea Airport is served by Fiji Link, the domestic arm of Fiji Airways, operating flights to and from Nadi and Suva on Viti Levu.

Q: How long is the flight from Nadi to Vunisea?
A: The flight from Nadi International Airport to Vunisea takes approximately 40-50 minutes on a turboprop aircraft.

Q: Is Vunisea Airport suitable for international flights?
A: No, Vunisea is a small domestic airport only and does not handle international flights. All international travelers must arrive at Nadi or Nausori (Suva) first.

Q: Are there facilities at the airport?
A: As a small rural airport, facilities are minimal, typically including a small terminal building and basic waiting areas. Travelers should arrange ground transport in advance.
transport_tips: Pre-arrange transport with your resort or hotel, as taxis and rental services are limited at the airport. The airport is a short drive from Vunisea village and nearby coastal resorts along Kadavu's main road. Driving the full length of Kadavu Island takes several hours, so plan accommodations accordingly.
local_tip: Pack light and bring reef-safe sunscreen, as Kadavu has minimal shopping facilities and the island's main attraction—the Great Astrolabe Reef—offers world-class diving and snorkeling that rewards those who come prepared.
